source.citation: Unidentified author, review of seventeen cases of cocaine taking, Medical Record 43 (1893): 34, summarising a case reported by Ring. Author, title, and Ring's original report to confirm.

complaints: growing sleeplessness and loss of appetite
unsteady nerves and a staggering gait
listless, with no interest in work or friends
presentation.course: Began a 4 per cent cocaine spray nightly for nasopharyngeal disease. After a month the effect lessened and he increased it. By the fourth month he used it more often, then four or five times before bed and once in the day.

findings: raised temperature and a quick heart

treatments.treatment: stopped on his own once he saw the drug had become a necessity

outcome: Quit; later course not reported in the summary.
quotes: using spray, four per cent, solution, nightly
becoming listless, no interest in work or friends

modernReading.text: Cocaine use disorder that began with a medical nasal spray. Tolerance, escalating dose, insomnia, weight loss, and a racing heart fit; the gait disturbance is less typical.

fixed: began with a cocaine spray or snuff for catarrh or hay fever
insomnia, poor appetite, listlessness, quick pulse

constrained.rule: comfortable or better; access to a physician's prescription or a druggist's catarrh cure
the patient hides or plays down the spray at first

notes: The same review quotes Atwood's case of a physician who became loud and boastful on cocaine snuff prescribed for a cold, and a case of three years' use for catarrh that recovered with massage and tonics in six weeks.
